    <item>
      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/global-development">Global development</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/senegal">Senegal</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/lgbt-rights">LGBTQ+ rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/human-rights">Human rights</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/anti-rights-movement">Anti-rights movement</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/africa">Africa</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/world">World news</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/law/law">Law</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/society/aids-and-hiv">Aids and HIV</category>
      <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:00:25 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5d08247e565b832f183d37b676fe7def25b19c25/213_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=123bd8ecc615f6c5a01371cef3492c23">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Jane Hahn/AP</media:credit>
      </media:content>
      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5d08247e565b832f183d37b676fe7def25b19c25/213_0_2500_2000/master/2500.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=add472ae1a295f31eda15f295087bdb3">

      <title>Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize</link>
      <description><p>Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</p><p></p><p>The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/israel-committed-genocide-in-gaza-says-un-inquiry">that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</a>.</p><p>The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:59:00 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Houthi attack on palace used by Yemen government in Aden kills five</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261015-houthi-attack-on-palace-used-by-yemen-government-in-aden-kills-five</link><description>
At least five people were killed and 16 wounded Thursday in a Houthi missile and drone attack on the palace located in Yemen's interim capital – the southern port city of Aden, used by the country's internationally recognised government, an official said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/726e8c4a-c8c3-11f1-b18b-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T171257Z-1450446933-RC2N3OAX74ZS-RTRMADP-3-SAUDI-YEMEN-ADEN-BOOMS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/726e8c4a-c8c3-11f1-b18b-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T171257Z-1450446933-RC2N3OAX74ZS-RTRMADP-3-SAUDI-YEMEN-ADEN-BOOMS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">27f1fba8-c8cc-11f1-b6d1-f56d77e2991f</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:57:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/726e8c4a-c8c3-11f1-b18b-2d1c143cdef3/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T171257Z-1450446933-RC2N3OAX74ZS-RTRMADP-3-SAUDI-YEMEN-ADEN-BOOMS.jpg">© Social media via Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Donald Trump 'openly financing Russia's war with Ukraine', Nobel peace laureate says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/donald-trump-openly-financing-russia-s-war-with-ukraine-nobel-peace-laureate-says</link><description>
Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Nobel Peace laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that with the diesel-supply deal with Moscow Donald Trump "is openly financing this war, by lifting sanctions is providing Russia with opportunities to earn more money" adding that "extra money will be converted in rockets and drones and additional deaths among the civilian population".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6dc8c71c-c8cf-11f1-b194-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-210633-211324-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6dc8c71c-c8cf-11f1-b194-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-210633-211324-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72e458d8-c8cf-11f1-b211-61fe1cac82d8</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:48:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Truth or Fake</category><title>Fake AI images of protester go viral after woman punched at Trump's Ohio rally</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/fake-ai-images-of-protester-go-viral-after-woman-punched-at-trump-s-ohio-rally</link><description>
A protester who heckled Donald Trump at his midterm rally in Youngstown, Ohio, was physically assaulted and removed from the event, but fake AI-generated photos recreating the incident are going viral online. The images carry digital watermarks identifying them as AI-generated. While footage confirms the woman was punched, there is no evidence to support Trump’s claim that the protester was "paid" to disrupt his speech, as he mocked the protester's weight. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b1970114-c8cc-11f1-8790-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-404d997e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b1970114-c8cc-11f1-8790-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-404d997e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1951dde4-c8cb-11f1-9ae9-77f3b18a7a98</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:47:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Vedika BAHL</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Seven missing off Romania after latest Black Sea drone attacks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/seven-missing-off-romania-after-latest-black-sea-drone-attacks</link><description>
Romania reported seven people missing on Thursday after two drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea, where several vessels have been hit recently in suspected fallout from the Ukraine war. The attacks are the latest in a series off the coast of Romania and neighbouring Bulgaria in recent weeks. FRANCE 24's Eliza Herbert reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8d4a8504-c8c9-11f1-bf1b-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-203417-203608-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8d4a8504-c8c9-11f1-bf1b-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-203417-203608-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">96ab9714-c8c9-11f1-8c3c-27acdd5cac97</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:04:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Albania's leader defies calls to resign as student protesters rampage in capital</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/albania-s-leader-defies-calls-to-resign-as-student-protesters-rampage-in-capital</link><description>
​Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Thursday rejected calls to resign as thousands of student-led protesters smashed windows and fought running battles with riot police firing water cannon and tear gas in the capital. The demonstrators accuse officials of corruption and neglecting education and say they are angry about the sale of parts of Albania's southern coastline to a luxury resort development backed ​by US President ‌Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/281c8484-c8c9-11f1-8ffe-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-200906-201102-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/281c8484-c8c9-11f1-8ffe-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261015-200906-201102-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">38d566e2-c8c9-11f1-b983-7f8e2f52719a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:02:14 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:13:26 +0000 en <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn ]]>

On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida.

It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn, with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005.

Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017.

Running low on fuel, NASA chose to steer Cassini straight into Saturn's atmosphere, where the spacecraft was destroyed.

Why it mattered

NASA's Cassini mission to Saturn (which carried the European Space Agency's Huygens lander to Titan) was a flagship planetary mission like no other ever when it first launched toward the ringed planet.

The $3.26 billion Cassini spacecraft became the first probe ever to orbit Saturn when it arrived in 2004. It revealed Saturn's rings as active and dynamic structures, as intricate and complex as they are beautiful to observe.

And it delivered Huygens to Titan, then followed up with a series of Titan flybys that revealed the cloudy moon could have liquid hydrocarbon rain, rivers, lakes and seas.

Perhaps the most exciting discoveries were the most surprising.

Cassini discovered a strange hexagon-shaped jetstream encircling Saturn's north pole and revealed massive hurricane-like vortexes over both of the planet's poles. In 2010, Cassini watched as a giant storm formed in Saturn's northern hemisphere, then grew to encircle the entire planet through 2011.

The spacecraft also discovered icy plumes of water erupting from Saturn's moon Enceladus, revealing new clues into that moon's subsurface ocean of liquid water, complete with hydrothermal events like those found in Earth's oceans.

It was to protect Enceladus, Titan and other Saturn moons that NASA ultimated sent Cassini into a death dive into Saturn at the end of its mission. The space agency wanted to prevent any chance of contamination at those pristine moons.

"NASA’s Cassini spacecraft and ESA’s Huygens probe expanded our understanding of the kinds of worlds where life might exist and eight more reasons the mission changed the course of planetary exploration," NASA said in an overview.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ Watch SpaceX launch classified mission for the US Space Force today ]]> SpaceX will launch a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force this evening (Oct. 15), and you can watch the action live.

A Falcon 9 rocket is scheduled to lift off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today, on California's beautiful but frequently fog-blanketed central coast, during a four-hour window that opens at 7:44 p.m. EDT (2344 GMT; 4:44 p.m. local time).

You can watch it live via a SpaceX webcast, which is expected to begin about 10 minutes before launch.

This evening's launch will kick off the USSF-481 mission, which will deliver mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier.

Don't expect SpaceX to provide more info during the webcast. It will probably end just after the Falcon 9 first stage's landing, which is expected to occur about eight minutes after launch on the drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

USSF-481 will be the 28th flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1081. Sixteen of its previous 27 launches were devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink broadband megaconstellation in low Earth orbit, according to a SpaceX mission description.

Previous Booster 1081 missions

Crew-7 | CRS-29 | PACE | Transporter-10 | EarthCARE | NROL-186 | Transporter-13 | TRACERS | NROL-48 | COSMO-SkyMed Second Generation FM3 | 16 Starlink missions

USSF-481 will be the 114th Falcon 9 mission of the year. The vast majority of the rocket's flights in 2026 — more than 70% of them — have been Starlink missions.

SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times so far this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but the fully reusable Starship remains in the test-flight phase. It reached orbit for the first time on its most recent launch, which occurred on Sept. 28.

]]> <![CDATA[ Vaonis unveils Atlas, the world's 1st modular smart telescope system ]]> Vaonis has just announced its new generation of smart telescope technology, known as Atlas. Less of a single smart telescope and more of a new optical system, Atlas was designed with interchangeability and adaptability in mind. Its new SkyDock system allows two optical tubes to be connected and the telescope has live night sky monitoring to predict available observations.

You can preorder the Vaonis Atlas with a single Atlas 80 module for $3,990, or $5,490 for the twin at Adorama. But it'll also soon be available at B&H and other retailers.

Currently, there is only one optical tube, the Atlas 80, but Vaonis is planning to release add-on modules designed for looking at different night sky objects, including for planetary observation. We think this is an exciting step for smart telescope technology and is, essentially, the start of modular astronomy for amateur stargazers, allowing them to choose optics that suit their observation interests. The Vaonis Atlas with two Atlas 80 modules will be available for preorder for $5,490.

Atlas with two Atlas 80 imaging modules: was $6990 now $5490
Pre-order and save $1,500 on the new Vaonis Atlas system that comes with two Atlas 80 imaging modules, a SkyGuard dock and a tripod.

Using dual imaging modules should enable faster imaging of deep sky objects.View Deal

Atlas with single Atlas 80 optical tube: was $4990 now $3990
Pre-order and save $1,000 on the new Vaonis Atlas system that comes with a single Atlas 80 imaging module, a SkyGuard dock and a tripod.

The dock contains an extra slot for dual module imaging, which can fit another Atlas 80 module and future optical tube releases.View Deal

  • We've got you covered with reviews and rankings of the best telescopes, binoculars, star projectors, cameras, drones, Lego, streaming and more.

The world of smart technology in stargazing optics is constantly pushing forward but it tends to move in waves in terms of actual "new" technology. Obviously, smart telescopes improve as new releases come out, usually with higher resolution and an upgraded optical design, but they are still just improvements on a base model. For years, Vaonis has improved and developed their Vespera models, but the announcement of the Atlas reveals a potential new direction for the company.

The Atlas system is the first-ever modular smart telescope system for Vaonis, with a base dock system fitted with two ports for connecting two imaging modules (an optical tube with a sensor). The Atlas 80 imaging module is an optical tube with a 3.15-in (80 mm) aperture and a Sony IMX585 8.3MP sensor, designed for imaging deep-space objects such as galaxies, nebulas and star clusters. Attaching identical imaging modules allows you to image targets quicker and with more detail, but the most intriguing part of this whole release is not actually available yet.

Vaonis has promised to expand the Atlas ecosystem after launch, including a backpack, filters, an equatorial wedge and most importantly, new imaging modules. The next planned imaging module is for planetary observation, which could be a game changer. If you have used a smart telescope for planetary observation, you will know that they produce grainy blobs when compared to their stunning deep space imagery. Vaonis might not just be introducing modularity for smart telescopes; they might also be introducing the ability to get a good photo of a planet with one.

Atlas pre-orders open today and are available from BH Photo and Video and Adorama. The special preorder pricing is available until Nov. 15, with the First shipments expected in March 2027. This release includes the SkyDock along with either one Atlas 80 or two Atlas 80 imaging modules.

Key features: Modular design, Atlas 80 imaging module with 3.15-in (80 mm) apochromatic quadruplet lens, 360 mm focal length, f/4.5 focal ratio and a Sony IMX585 8.3-megapixel sensor, app-controlled, automatic pointing and imaging (Go-To function), 16.1-in (41 cm) height when closed (excluding tripod), 14.3 lb (6.5 kg) weight, up to 6 hours of battery life.

Product launched: Oct 2026

Price comparison for Vaonis Atlas with single optical tube: B&H PhotoVideo: Likely starting at $3,990 | Adorama: Starting at $3,990

✅ Buy it if: You want to invest in a smart telescope but are interested in getting the best photographs of a wide range of night sky targets, including deep-space objects and planets.

❌ Don't buy it if: You don't care about interchangeability or adaptability from your smart telescope and are mainly interested in using it to photograph deep-sky objects.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA's SkyFall helicopters will 'show us parts of Mars we've never seen before', scientists say ]]> NASA is accelerating the development of three helicopters that will be deployed into the sky above Mars after a voyage aboard NASA's Space Reactor‑1 Freedom spacecraft.

Slated for launch in 2028, SR-1 Freedom is the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft and is assigned the duty of dropping off the SkyFall entry capsule loaded with the trio of aerial vehicles at the Red Planet. SR-1's trajectory will deliver the SkyFall helicopters in Mars' northern hemisphere during the planet's spring season to avoid dust storms.

SkyFall is based on the success of the first aerial craft to float about the Red Planet, Ingenuity, which flew over 70 missions at Jezero Crater before it finally broke a rotor. It was designed to fly five. The SkyFall mission will consist of three identical helicopters to be deployed by an entry vehicle in the atmosphere, let loose at roughly under a mile (3,300 feet or 1,000 meters) above Mars, with each of the craft landing independently.

Regions of interest

The SkyFall mission is to conduct investigations that address objectives relevant for science and preparing for human exploration of Mars. Anticipated flights of the vehicles will travel outside of the landing ellipse to regions of interest within a broader exploration zone.

However, there are further science-focused flight paths and regions that have yet to be determined. NASA intends for the SkyFall helicopters to go to multiple regions of scientific interest on Mars.

NASA's Mars Exploration Program, along with the SkyFall project at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), will work together to pick those "why and where" paths to navigate.

A first workshop on potential landing sites for the SkyFall mission and adjacent exploration zones of high scientific value is slated for early next year. And as always, sites and zones on Mars for the choppers means satisfying engineering constraints imposed by the project and spacecraft design.

Given the rapid development cadence of the SkyFall mission, decisions are to be fast-paced, but are geared to maximizing science value of the endeavor.

What Mars researchers are after will be a ranked list of potential landing sites that will be studied in more detail by the SkyFall project and science community, prior to a second workshop to be held in late 2027.

Notional flight trajectories

On the table are potential science value and notional flight trajectories of individual landing sites given the capabilities and payload of the SkyFall helicopters.

Landing site selection will occur after the back-to-back landing site workshops next year, said Matthew Golombek, SkyFall Project Scientist at JPL.

"The project has identified a design reference landing site that targets subsurface water ice deposits with glacial/periglacial terrains," Golombek told Space.com.

Given their deployment, how much real estate will the aerial vessel assault study?

Golombek said that the helicopters are capable of flying one to two kilometers every other sol, so flight traverses of 125 miles to a little over 185 miles (200-300 kilometers) are possible.

"The helicopters are designed to last 6 months, with a goal of one Earth year and each can fly every other sol so multiple flights are expected," Golombek added.

Thanks to the success of the Perseverance rover's unleashing of the Ingenuity rotorcraft, Golombek said that there are a host of lessons learned, as well as engineering additions to be made to the set of SkyFall vehicles.

Nominal payload

"Although the helicopters are slightly larger than Ingenuity, they are being designed to operate in exactly the same way, so all of the experience with Ingenuity operations will be directly relevant," said Golombek.

The nominal payload to be toted around the Red Planet will be identical for all three helicopters, consisting of five instruments, plus engineering navigation cameras. Those instruments are to investigate the subsurface structure of Mars, the geomorphology and geology of surface terrains, as well as look at the meteorology of the atmosphere and the radiation environment.

Although there is no dedicated hardware to directly measure winds, the helicopters themselves can serve as on-the-spot wind sensors, even shifting to "Balloon Mode," whereby a helicopter will drift in the background wind.

Radar love

Each low-flying helicopter is outfitted with a ground penetrating radar (GPR) instrument, one that can detect layering in the near surface, at depths unobservable by orbital radar.

Those layers could be assembled from rocky material, buried ice, or combinations of the two. Detection of near-surface ice is of interest both scientifically as well as in support of future human expeditions to Mars.

Subsurface ice not only preserves a record of past Martian climate but also serves as a "high-priority environment" that might have served as a habitat of past…or Martian life resident today.

SkyFall maneuver

AeroVironment of Arlington, Virginia is partnering with JPL, selected last August to co-design and co-manufacture the SkyFall helicopters. They too are building on their experience as co‑developers of NASA's Ingenuity Mars helicopter that made those 72 flights at Jezero Crater on Mars.

"Now, with SkyFall, we're taking AV's high‑volume uncrewed systems mindset into planetary exploration and showing that Mars helicopters can be built as a repeatable product line, not a one‑off delivery," said Jeff Rodrian, Head of MacCready Works, AV's advanced research and development organization.

A special "SkyFall maneuver" is to be utilized in deploying the three aerial craft. They will be released directly from the carrier spacecraft into the Martian atmosphere, where they separate, deploy, descend, and land under their own power.

"By eliminating the need for a single-use lander stage or a host rover (as Ingenuity required with Perseverance), this approach significantly reduces the technical and financial risk of getting to the Martian surface," explains an AeroVironment statement.

Mountains of data

"Just like here on Earth, Mars helicopters can cover distance quickly and can go places that might be impossible to reach by ground," said Will Pomerantz, Head of Space Ventures at AeroVironment.

The science community may guide these helicopters to locations, Pomerantz said, where the ground penetrating radar can map out the specific spots of ice below the martian surface.

"The three SkyFall helicopters are going to show us parts of Mars we've never seen before and return mountains of data for scientists to pore over," said Pomerantz.

]]> <![CDATA[ Windblown yardangs on Mars | Space photo of the day for Oct. 15, 2026 ]]>

A new image from the European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft reveals the powerful erosive forces that have shaped and re-shaped the surface of the Red Planet over long periods of geological time.

What is it?

This new Mars Express image captures Amazonis Mensa, a large, flat mountain on the Red Planet that offers planetary scientists a glimpse into the many factors that can sculpt a world's surface.

In this photograph, several features stand out to help illustrate this. Easiest to make out are the large round craters created by ancient impacts on the surface of Mars. However, many of these craters have been at least partially filled by lava flowing across the surface of the Red Planet around three billion years ago, according a statement from the European Space Agency (ESA) accompanying the image.

More interestingly, rippled structures known as yardangs can be seen to the left and right sides of the image. These ridges "form as loose sand particles are whipped up by wind and deployed a little like a cosmic sandblaster," according to ESA.

In the image, the two groups of yardangs ripple across the Martian surface in two different directions. This is because Amazonis Mensa acts as a windbreak, pushing material blown by winds in separate orientations.

Why is it incredible?

For over 20 years, Mars Express has been providing scientists with an unparalleled look at the Martian surface, helping us better understand the forces that have shaped the Red Planet over eons.

]]> <![CDATA[ Scientists discover 'chemical starter kit' for life in planetary birthplaces ]]> Methanol, coming as part of the 'chemical starter kit' around young stars, has produced some unexpected surprises that could ultimately reveal some of the conditions in which planets and potentially life form around protostars.

The methanol discoveries were made by astronomers using ALMA (the Atacama Large millimeter/submillimeter Array) in the Atacama Desert in Chile, as part of a project called COMPASS (the Complex Organic Molecules in Protostars with ALMA Spectral Surveys).

"Our work provides insight into the complex chemistry of young star systems and is ultimately an important piece of the puzzle in understanding the origin of life," said University of Bern astrophysicist Maria Drozdovskaya, who leads the COMPASS project, in a statement.

Drozdovskaya's multinational team of more than 30 astronomers has been chasing down complex organic molecules, large molecules that include carbon atoms, in the planetary construction yards around eleven young stars.

These molecules form part of the chemical inventory that ultimately builds planets and, perhaps, even life that will one day live on those planets.

Methanol matters

Methanol (CH3OH) is important because it is highly abundant in star- and planet-forming regions. In fact, it’s the most abundant complex organic molecule to be found in interstellar space, and is commonly found in planet-forming disks.

Its sheer abundance means that, of all the molecules found around young stars, methanol is the easiest in which to detect different forms where regular hydrogen atoms are replaced by a heavier isotope of hydrogen called deuterium.

How many molecules contain these heavier isotopes is highly dependent upon the conditions in which planets are forming within the disk.

That’s why the COMPASS team used ALMA to search for these forms of methanol in the gas belonging to the planet-forming disks around the 11 nearby low-mass protostars. The observations have also helped assess the general chemical diversity of these disks.

The unexpected discovery of a methanol molecule containing deuterium was made in the planet-forming disk around only one of those 11 stars, namely the young star IRAS 4A2, located about a thousand light-years away in the Perseus Molecular Cloud.

IRAS refers to the Infrared Astronomical Satellite, which was a joint NASA–UK–Netherlands mission launched in 1983 and which first detected this young star as a source of infrared light through the thick gas and dust of the molecular cloud.

The COMPASS team also discovered methanol maser emission from more than half of the 11 protostars, favoring the youngest of the stars. A maser is a microwave version of a laser in the sense that the microwave emission is being stimulated and then amplified, but astrophysical masers occur naturally, often in shock fronts as methanol molecules collide and are excited.

Methanol masers have previously been detected in planet-forming disks around turbulent high-mass protostars, but COMPASS’ observations are the first detection of them around calmer lower-mass protostars.

"The fact that it has now also been found in a low-mass protostar shows that locally extreme physical conditions can prevail there analogously to massive stars and challenges our previous understanding of the formation of sun-like stars," said Drozdovskaya.

The finding implies that methanol masers are a common product of all planet-forming discs and therefore are produced by processes that are universal in star- and planet-birth, regardless of the protostar's mass.

For example, thermal bursts from the growing star as it accumulates gas from its surroundings could generate shocks in a planet-forming disk, stimulating maser activity in the abundant methanol.

"Both results underscore how important high-performance spectroscopic measurements like those from COMPASS with ALMA are for detecting rare and previously unknown chemical phenomena," said Drozdovskaya, referring to both the methanol masers and the deuterium-rich methanol molecules around IRAS 4A2. "They show just how much we still have to learn about the chemical processes in young protostellar systems."

The new findings have at least begun to answer some questions, such as how the diversity in this 'chemical starter kit' varies from star to star, with ALMA detecting some subtle differences, such as variations in the abundance of oxygen- and nitrogen-bearing molecular species among the eleven stars.

However, questions about how the chemistry of young star systems arises and how it influences the evolution of those systems remain unanswered.

For now, the COMPASS team is painstakingly and systematically studying the data on all the different types of molecules detected in their ALMA observations, and preparing follow-up studies with other facilities including the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

"The analysis of all the collected data will take several more years," said Drozdovskaya.

The first results from COMPASS are published in seven papers [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] in the October 2026 issue of the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX wants to launch Starship more than 450 times per year from South Texas ]]> SpaceX wants to start flying its Starship megarocket a lot more often.

The company has requested permission to launch Starship from its Starbase site in South Texas up to 456 times per year. That's a big jump from the currently allowed cadence of 25.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is in the early stages of reviewing the request. Today (Oct. 14), the agency announced "its intent to prepare a Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, open a public scoping period and hold public scoping meetings for SpaceX’s proposal."

Starship, which stands more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall, is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. It's also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX believes will revolutionize spaceflight.

The megarocket has flown 14 times to date, all of them test flights from Starbase, which is near the Texas border city of Brownsville. On the most recent jaunt, which lifted off on Sept. 28, Starship reached orbit for the first time and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites — the first members of a new broadband constellation that could eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft.

Assembling that network will require a lot of Starship launches. And even more will be needed to build SpaceX's planned Starmind AI megaconstellation, which Elon Musk has said will harbor a million satellites. Indeed, the world's richest man has said that SpaceX is targeting more than 10,000 Starship liftoffs per year by 2030.

Not all of those flights will originate from Starbase, which hosts two orbital pads. SpaceX is working to get three Starship pads up and running on Florida's Space Coast, and the company aims to break ground on a $100 billion, 12-pad complex in Louisiana next year.

Each operational Starship launch will also feature two landings. Both of the vehicle's elements — the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — are designed to return to the pad after liftoff, where they will be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. So SpaceX's proposal for 456 launches from Starbase per year includes a request for approval for 912 landings.

SpaceX plans to work up to this cadence in two phases, according to the FAA. Phase 1 "would include up to 100 annual launches and up to 200 annual landings (100 of Starship and 100 of Super Heavy)," the agency wrote. "Launches and landings could occur any day or time of the week."

Phase 2 covers 456 launches and 912 landings, which would occur only Monday through Friday, though at any time on those days.

The FAA will hold five "public scoping meetings" about the proposal next month, four of them in person in the Starbase area and one of them virtual.

SpaceX wants to start flying its Starship megarocket a lot more often.

The company has requested permission to launch Starship from its Starbase site in South Texas up to 456 times per year. That's a big jump from the currently allowed cadence of 25.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is in the early stages of reviewing the request. Today (Oct. 14), the agency announced "its intent to prepare a Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, open a public scoping period and hold public scoping meetings for SpaceX’s proposal."

Starship, which stands more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall, is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. It's also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX believes will revolutionize spaceflight.

The megarocket has flown 14 times to date, all of them test flights from Starbase, which is near the Texas border city of Brownsville. On the most recent jaunt, which lifted off on Sept. 28, Starship reached orbit for the first time and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites — the first members of a new broadband constellation that could eventually consist of 100,000 spacecraft.

Assembling that network will require a lot of Starship launches. And even more will be needed to build SpaceX's planned Starmind AI megaconstellation, which Elon Musk has said will harbor a million satellites. Indeed, the world's richest man has said that SpaceX is targeting more than 10,000 Starship liftoffs per year by 2030.

Not all of those flights will originate from Starbase, which hosts two orbital pads. SpaceX is working to get three Starship pads up and running on Florida's Space Coast, and the company aims to break ground on a $100 billion, 12-pad complex in Louisiana next year.

Each operational Starship launch will also feature two landings. Both of the vehicle's elements — the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — are designed to return to the pad after liftoff, where they will be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. So SpaceX's proposal for 456 launches from Starbase per year includes a request for approval for 912 landings.

SpaceX plans to work up to this cadence in two phases, according to the FAA. Phase 1 "would include up to 100 annual launches and up to 200 annual landings (100 of Starship and 100 of Super Heavy)," the agency wrote. "Launches and landings could occur any day or time of the week."

Phase 2 covers 456 launches and 912 landings, which would occur only Monday through Friday, though at any time on those days.

The FAA will hold five "public scoping meetings" about the proposal next month, four of them in person in the Starbase area and one of them virtual.

There will be two in-person meetings on Nov. 17 at Texas Southmost College, one from 1-3 p.m. local (Central) time and the other from 5:30-7:30 p.m. Two in-person meetings will follow on Nov. 19, at the same two times but at a different location: the Port Isabel Event & Cultural Center.

The virtual meeting will be held Nov. 18, from 5:30-7:30 p.m. Central time. Registration is required for all of these meetings, even the virtual one. You can register here.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX Cargo Dragon delivers more than 6,000 pounds of supplies to the ISS ]]>

A Dragon has settled into its nest after a more than two-day-long orbital pursuit.

SpaceX's cargo Dragon, flying the CRS-35 (35th Commercial Resupply Services) mission for NASA, rendezvoused with the International Space Station (ISS) this morning (Oct. 15), delivering fresh food, long-term provisions, research and hardware to the orbital lab and its crew.

Coverage of Dragon's arrival at the ISS began at 9:00 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT), as the spacecraft approached from approximately 2.3 miles (3.6 km) away. NASA astronaut Anil Menon served as the station's prime crew member this morning, responsible for monitoring Dragon's approach and autonomous procedures. Docking occurred with the space-face port of the station's Harmony module at 10:27 a.m. EDT (1427 GMT), as the ISS flew about 250 miles (400 km) above South Africa, traveling around 17,500 mph (28,000 kph).

Dragon's arrival brings more than 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of food, research equipment and other supplies, including flight support equipment to replace components on the Canadarm2, a toilet dose pump, a toilet pretreat quality sensor, a robot micro-conical tool used for station maintenance and the very last of eight upgraded solar panels designed to augment the station's power capabilities.

In addition to the usual provisions carried on this mission, Dragon also brought a special suprise for Menon, who is celebrating his 50th birthday today, according to NASA's broadcast spokesperson.

CRS-35 launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the company's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Tuesday (Oct. 13). Liftoff occurred at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), and the Falcon 9's upper stage deployed the Dragon in low Earth orbit (LEO) a short 10 minutes later. Thanks to the trajectory of the space station's orbit and the near-dawn hour of the launch, the Falcon 9's ascent to orbit was viewed by millions up and down the U.S. East Coast, who witnessed a rare "space jellyfish" phenomenon from the rocket's exhaust plume.

The supplies delivered on CRS-35 will largely support the station's newest astronaut inhabitants, the members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission for NASA. The four-person crew arrived aboard the ISS on Oct. 1, relieving the members of Crew-12, who returned to Earth a week later.

Crew-12 astronauts will address the media this afternoon (Oct. 15) to discuss their mission and their return after nearly eight months on orbit. A live broadcast of that event will also be available to stream on Space.com's homepage beginning at 3:30 p.m. EDT (1930 GMT).

Cargo Dragon's nominal orbital insertion on Tuesday placed it on course to catch up with the ISS after a 51-hour LEO chase. After rendezvous this morning, Dragon will autonomously dock to the zenith port on the station's Harmony module. It will remain docked with the ISS for about a month before being packed with supplies, waste and research for its return, safe splashdown and recovery on Earth.

]]> <![CDATA[ Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 'families,' scientists find ]]> You can tell a lot about how a child will age by looking at their parents, and it turns out that this could be true for planetary systems, too. Scientists have performed cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.

The study team, led by researchers at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), studied 300 of the best-understood multiplanet systems of the over 1,000 that astronomers have discovered in the Milky Way.

The team's research clarifies how the environments around infant stars directly affect planetary fates and, in turn, the survival of extrasolar planets, or exoplanets, that are potentially capable of hosting life. That could be crucial as astronomers search for life beyond the solar system, pointing them to systems with potentially habitable planets like Earth.

"The fundamental question we started from was: What determines the characteristics of planetary systems as we see them today? Are they established at birth or sculpted by evolution over time? The truth, in the end, turned out to lie somewhere in the middle," team member and INAF researcher Diego Turrini said in a statement sent to Space.com.

"Our results show that there is a genetic link between planetary systems and their stars, and that, depending on the star around which they are born, this link also determines their fate," Turrini added.

What is the genetic code of a planetary system?

The first "family" the scientists identified consists of wide, massive systems, often with total masses between two and 10 times that of our own solar system. The planets in these systems orbit stars more massive than the sun with lower concentrations of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium (which astronomers somewhat confusingly call metals) than seen in our star.

The second family is more compact and lower-mass systems. The members of this family are composed of planets with comparable masses and sizes, a so-called "peas-in-a-pod" configuration. They orbit stars with mass and metallicity equal to or lower than those of the sun, with orbits that are usually much tighter than those of Mercury, the closest planet to the sun.

One of the "genes" Turrini and colleagues selected to sort planetary systems into families was the deviations that planets make from orbiting their star in the same circular plane. That, in turn, reveals a family history of violent gravitational instability caused by events like giant collisions and planetary ejections.

Violent events were common for the first family, but much less so for the second group of planetary systems, the researchers found. They determined that the number of these turbulent events a planetary system experiences can be linked to even modest variations in the environment in which planets form. These variations arise due to different properties of the parent star of those systems.

Thus, the nature of the star in these systems doesn't just fundamentally change the formation of planets in their systems; it influences the system's future evolution, determining whether it will be characterized by phases of marked instability and giant impacts.

"The main difficulty during the data analysis was determining whether the two families of planetary systems were real or just an illusion created by the technological limits of current observational techniques," said team member Camilla Danielski, of the University of Valencia in Spain.

"At the end of the path, it became clear that selection effects acted as the tip of the iceberg, revealing the existence of much deeper structural diversities between these systems," Danielski said.

The scientists tested their conclusions by running simulations of planetary system evolution, all of which began with different conditions.

"The scenarios that best reproduce the dynamical properties of the family of wide and massive systems are those in which the systems are unstable from birth," said research supervisor and INAF researcher Danae Polychroni. "The greater abundance of material from which planets form around their host stars causes them to be born too large, preventing the system from remaining stable."

The team's research was published on Tuesday (Oct. 13) in the journal Nature Astronomy.

  <item>
   <title>XFG není nová varianta covidu, říká viroložka. Příznaky má ale specifické</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/zdravotnictvi/zdravi-covid-xfg-priznaky-chrapot-paleni-v-krku-kasel/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zdravotnictvi</link>
   <description>Subvarianta covidu XFG, známá jako Stratus, nyní dominuje v Evropě i u nás. Ačkoli ji někteří označují za novou či americkou mutaci, virologové upozorňují, že cirkuluje již od minulého roku. Současné vakcíny ji obsahují jako vakcinační kmen. Odborníci doporučují očkování rizikovým skupinám, přičemž zdůrazňují vhodné načasování vzhledem k nadcházející chřipkové sezóně. Hlavními příznaky jsou pálení v krku, chrapot a kašel. Deník.cz přináší přehled nejčastejších otázek spojených s covidem XFG.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 13:51:36 +0200</pubDate>

   <title>Babí léto se vrátí, tvrdí meteorologové. Ještě předtím ale přijde teplotní šok</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/pocasi/predpoved-pocasi-cesko-okraje-babi-leto-nekonci-prijde-ale-ochlazeni-zlom-radar/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=pocasi</link>
   <description>Konec pracovního týdne přinese změnu charakteru počasí. Zatímco v pátek mohou teploty někde atakovat i „dvacítku“, o víkendu se citelně ochladí a teplotní rozdíl může být i deset stupňů Celsia. Kromě toho přibude oblačnost a místy se objeví slabé přeháňky. Teplým a slunečným dnům ale rozhodně není konec a do Česka se po víkendové přestávce vrátí babí léto. Sucho se tak bude nadále prohlubovat.</description>

  <item>
   <title>U zámku v Zákupech začala obnova další části hospodářského dvora za 242 milionů</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/u-zamku-v-zakupech-zacala-obnova-dalsi-casti-hospodarskeho-dvora-za-242-milionu/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>U státního zámku v Zákupech předáním staveniště začala obnova další části hospodářského dvora z konce 17. století, který je národní kulturní památkou. Stát bude 242 milionů korun a práce potrvají do roku 2029. Obnovené prostory budou sloužit jako zázemí zámku a do doby zřízení depozitáře také pro uložení archeologických nálezů.   </description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 12:04:57 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/u-zamku-v-zakupech-zacala-obnova-dalsi-casti-hospodarskeho-dvora-za-242-milionu/</guid>
   <category>Českolipsko </category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/f9f/f9fa1089-3db2-414d-9b7f-40080e0d0298.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/f9f/f9fa1089-3db2-414d-9b7f-40080e0d0298.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Hospodářský dvůr zámku v Zákupech, kde začala obnova jižní části a západního křídla, ve kterém byl v minulosti pivovar. </media:description>
    <media:credit>Petra Hámová</media:credit>

  <item>
   <title>Platit si jídlo a pobyt v domově důchodců ze svého? Návrh vyvolal smršť reakcí</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/ekonomika-domovy-duchodcu-navrh-platit-si-jidlo-ubytovani-/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Jídlo a ubytování v domovech seniorů a obdobných zařízeních za své, případně s pomocí rodiny? Návrh Asociace poskytovatelů sociálních služeb ČR, o kterém Deník.cz nedávno informoval a k němuž se ministerští úředníci staví rezervovaně, vyvolal mezi čtenáři zájem i polemiky. Přinášíme proto další informace včetně názorů lidí z oboru. Shodují se na tom, že systém musí mít jasná pravidla a o péči nesmí přijít chudší senioři.</description>
   <pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 07:00:00 +0200</pubDate>

      <title>Pavel se vrátil z Maroka. Do Prahy přiletěl linkou, tryskáč si nakonec rozmyslel</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/petr-pavel-dovolena-prezident-cesko-navrat-maroko-letiste-letadlo.A261015_172931_domaci_svm#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Prezident Petr Pavel se vrátil z dovolené v Maroku. Do Prahy po kritice tentokrát nepřiletěl soukromým tryskáčem, ale linkou nízkonákladové společnosti Ryanair. Podle informací iDNES.cz se Pavel vydal na cestu z marockého mezinárodního letiště Nador zhruba ve 12 hodin tamního času. Let byl s přestupem v Marseille.</description>

      <title>Srážka autobusu s nákladním vlakem u Eurotunelu. Zraněných jsou dvě desítky</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/eurotunel-razka-autobus-vlak.A261015_213551_zahranicni_dvou#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>U vjezdu do Eurotunelu na francouzské straně se srazil autobus s nákladním vlakem. Zraněno bylo 19 lidí, provoz tunelu je přerušen. Nikdo ze zraněných není v ohrožení života, uvedly francouzské úřady.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Chceme víc pro zdravotníky, žádají odbory. Vojtěch zvýšení o 12 miliard odmítá</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/odbory-rust-mezd-zdravotniku-adam-vojtech.A261015_204102_ekonomika_onbu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Odbory žádají úpravu návrhu úhradové vyhlášky na příští rok, aby umožnila růst platů a mezd v nemocnicích a zdravotnické záchranné službě (ZZS) nejméně o šest procent. Podle jejich výpočtu by bylo potřeba 12 miliard korun. Řekla to předsedkyně Odborového svazu zdravotnictví a sociální péče ČR Dagmar Žitníková. </description>

    <item>
      <title>Volali v Austrálii na tísňovou linku marně. Při čekání na pomoc zemřeli</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/australie-optus-pripad-dvou-muzu-zachranna-sluzba.A261015_184711_zahranicni_onbu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Úřady ve státě Queensland na severovýchodě Austrálie začaly vyšetřovat samostatné případy dvou pacientů, kteří v uplynulém týdnu zemřeli při čekání na lékařskou péči. Třiapadesátiletý muž, který pociťoval bolesti na hrudi, zavolal v sobotu večer na tísňovou linku 000 ze svého domu v Annerley na předměstí města Brisbane.</description>

      <description>Po srážce s vlakem zemřel ve čtvrtek večer řidič osobního auta. Nehoda se stala na železničním přejezdu u Bítovan na Chrudimsku. Podle dosavadních informací nikdo z cestujících ve vlaku neutrpěl zranění, uvedla mluvčí krajské policie Iveta Kopecká.</description>

      <title>Nastává osudová hodina Ukrajiny: došly patrioty, Rusko chystá definitivní zkázu</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajine-dosly-patrioty-rusko-chce-zemi-rozdrtit-v-prubehu-zimy.A261015_192008_zahranicni_remy#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Rusko chce Ukrajinu rozdrtit a vynutit si její úplnou kapitulaci ještě letos v zimě tím, že vyřadí z provozu ukrajinský energetický systém a zcela připraví Kyjev, Charkov a Oděsu o vodu, elektřinu a teplo. „Je téměř nemožné donutit zemi ke kapitulaci pouze konvenční leteckou kampaní ve válce. Zdá se, že Rusko je odhodláno to zkusit,“ napsal ve čtvrtek list The New York Times (NYT). Televize CNN mezitím informovala, že Ukrajině došly rakety Patriot.</description>

      <description>Jemenští proíránští povstalci Húsíové vypálili několik raket na prezidentský palác v jihojemenském Adenu, kam se v roce 2015 uchýlila mezinárodně uznávaná vláda. Dva vládní představitelé řekli, že jemenský premiér a ministři, kteří byli v prezidentském komplexu, vyvázli bez újmy. Zabiti však podle nich byli dva členové ostrahy.     <item>
      <title>Mezinárodní energetická agentura urychlí uvolnění nouzových zásob ropy</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/zahranicni/iea-rezervy-ropa-nafra-zasoby-trh.A261015_183226_eko-zahranicni_dvou#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Mezinárodní energetická agentura (IEA) se dohodla, že co nejdříve uvolní na trh více než 20 milionů barelů nafty a veškerou ropu, které zbývají z rekordního uvolnění nouzových zásob slíbeného v březnu. Cílem opatření je zmírnit nedostatek paliv a snížit ceny, které prudce vzrostly kvůli narušení dodávek z Blízkého východu a Ruska.</description>

<title>Ondřej Vlček znovu oficiálně ve světové kybernetické lize, startup Aisle bude kupovat kanadská firma</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/ondrej-vlcek-znovu-oficialne-ve-svetove-kyberneticke-lize-startup-aisle-bude-kupovat-kanadska-firma/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Pražský kyberbezpečnostní startup Aisle, za nímž stojí Ondřej Vlček, Stanislav Fort a Jaya Ballo, hodlá koupit kanadská AI společnost Cohere. Praha má být evropskou základnou firmy.  <description>Poprava někdejšího armádního psychiatra Nidala Hasana, který v roce 2009 zabil na vojenské základně v Texasu 13 lidí a dalších 32 zranil, nakonec nebude přenášena živě. Na své sociální síti Truth Social to ve čtvrtek oznámil americký prezident Donald Trump. Dodal, že vojenskou popravu, která bude provedena zastřelením popravčí četou, budou moci sledovat rodiny obětí.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/navrh-rozpoctu-evropske-unie-je-pod-vahou-kritiky-shoda-na-summitu-je_2610151620_brz</link>
 <description>Návrhy Evropské komise na nové zdroje budoucího rozpočtu Evropské unie jsou pro Česko naprosto nepřijatelné, uvedl premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) před čtvrtečním začátkem summitu Evropské unie. Jeho hlavním tématem má být právě návrh sedmiletého hospodaření EU, s jehož irskou verzí jsou mnohé země stále nespokojené. „Od současného summitu bych dohodu neočekával,“ říká pro Radiožurnál Filip Křenek, výzkumný spolupracovník institutu Europeum.</description>

 <description>Americký miliardář Elon Musk napsal na své sociální síti X, že za omezením družicové služby Starshield, která poskytuje podporu ukrajinské armádě, může být administrativa Donalda Trumpa. O provozu tohoto systému rozhoduje velení amerických ozbrojených sil. „Musk sice podporuje Starshield pro obranu Ukrajiny, ale odmítá jakoukoli eskalaci a tvrdí, že má dojít k mírovému řešení,“ říká pro Radiožurnál šéfredaktor serveru 365tipu.cz Daniel Dočekal.</description>

 <description>Rakouský soud propustil z vazby Slováka, který čelí obviněním z otravy výživ potravinářské společnosti HiPP, aby ji tak vydíral. Informovala o tom agentura APA. Slovák, který už dříve vinu odmítl, po dobu nadcházejícího procesu nesmí opustit Rakousko.</description>

 <title>Postavit kryt je teď v Polsku snazší než cokoliv jiného, říká starosta města Malbork, kde je staví jako první </title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/postavit-kryt-je-ted-v-polsku-snazsi-nez-cokoliv-jineho-rika-starosta-mesta_2610151356_jar</link>
 <description>Polská vláda schválila dalších skoro 560 miliard korun na civilní obranu. Investice v následujících pěti letech poslouží k výstavbě civilních krytů, k nákupu záchranného a zdravotnického vybavení nebo k vybudování výstražného systému a bezpečné komunikace. Program ochrany obyvatelstva a civilní obrany funguje v Polsku od loňského roku a čerpá z něj například Malbork. Jako první v Polsku nyní buduje moderní protichemické a protiatomové kryty.</description>

</item>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/stopka-pro-spisovatelku-rooneyovou-kvuli-podpore-palestincu-se-v-britanii_2610151354_ako</link>
 <description>Ve Velké Británii se přestanou prodávat knihy irské spisovatelky Sally Rooneyové kvůli jejímu záměru použít výnosy pro propalestinskou skupinu Palestine Action, jež Londýn zakázal jako teroristickou organizaci. Autorka i nakladatelství Faber to oznámily ve středu. Ten uvedl, že mu zákony neumožňují předávat Rooneyové příjmy z prodeje knih v Británii, proto se v Británii prodávat nebudou. Jinde budou dostupné, informovaly agentury Reuters a AP.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/uploader/2026-10-14t151142z_1_261015-133442_ako.JPG?itok=OQNusKEn" type="image/jpeg" />

</item>
<item>
 <title>Trump a jeho poradci zvažují, jak ukončit válku v Íránu. Mezi možnostmi je i ‚matka všech bomb‘</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/trump-a-jeho-poradci-zvazuji-jak-ukoncit-valku-v-iranu-mezi-moznostmi-je-i-matka_2610151344_raf</link>
 <description>Ozbrojené síly USA vypracovaly nové plány úderů na Írán, které zahrnují možné použití jejich nejsilnější nejaderné bomby GBU-43/B, přezdívané „matka všech bomb“. S odvoláním na informované zdroje to ve čtvrtek napsal web stanice CNN. Plány připravené pro případné rozhodnutí prezidenta Donalda Trumpa obnovit vojenské operace před listopadovými volbami do Kongresu či po nich mezi cíle útoků zařadily jaderná zařízení a energetickou infrastrukturu.</description>

</item>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/loni-jsme-meli-volby-ne-revoluci-albansky-premier-odmitl-rezignovat-navzdory_2610151239_med</link>
 <description>Albánský premiér Edi Rama odmítl odstoupit z funkce navzdory násilným studentským protestům, které zemí zmítají již třetím dnem. Demonstranti kritizují současnou vládu a stav školství a žádají demisi šéfa vlády. Rama podle agentury Reuters zdůraznil, že nedovolí, aby násilnosti zmařily snahu Albánie o vstup do Evropské unie.</description>

 <description>Ukrajina v noci na čtvrtek zaútočila na vojenské letiště Borisoglebsk v ruské Voroněžské oblasti a zasáhla šest bombardérů Suchoj Su-34M, oznámilo na facebooku ukrajinské námořnictvo a uvedlo, že k útoku použilo střely Neptun.</description>

Zpříjemněte si vánoční svátky koncertem v barokní konírně zámku Zákupy! V neděli 27. prosince 2026 zde vystoupí Michal Volf, který připomene nezapomenutelné hity Karla Gotta. Těšit se můžete na známé melodie i příjemnou sváteční atmosféru.

]]> Thu, 15 Oct 2026 12:49:19 GMT <![CDATA[Chalupa Kořenov 10]]>

Horská chalupa Kořenov 10 na pomezí Jizerských hor a Krkonoš, s tradicí sahající až do roku 1730, nabízí ubytování až pro 38 osob v klidné přírodě. Je ideálním zázemím pro rodiny s dětmi, skupiny přátel, školy, sportovní kluby i firemní akce.

]]> Wed, 14 Oct 2026 23:14:25 GMT <![CDATA[Svět fantazie ve Státním muzeu skla a bižuterie v Jablonci nad Nisou]]>

Státní muzeum skla a bižuterie v Jablonci nad Nisou zve na výstavu Svět fantazie v novém návštěvnickém depozitáři skleněných vánočních ozdob.

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Dýně v neděli zaplní centrum Liberce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903090-dyne-v-nedeli-zaplni-centrum-liberce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903090-dyne-v-nedeli-zaplni-centrum-liberce.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 20:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Náměstí před libereckou radnicí promění v místo podzimní atmosféry, vůní a chutí. Od 10 do 16 hodin se zde uskuteční tradiční Dýňová neděle. Akce nabídne speciální nejen dýňový trh, kulinářskou soutěž, ochutnávky i bohatý doprovodný program pro děti i dospělé. Vstup je zdarma.</description></item><item><title>V Kauflandu v Jablonci našli inspektoři výživu dřív stahovanou z prodeje kvůli toxinu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903149-v-kauflandu-v-jablonci-nasli-inspektori-vyzivu-driv-stahovanou-z-prodeje-kvuli-toxinu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903149-v-kauflandu-v-jablonci-nasli-inspektori-vyzivu-driv-stahovanou-z-prodeje-kvuli-toxinu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 18:53:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Kojenecké výživy značky Nutrilon, dříve stahované z prodeje kvůli podezření na výskyt toxinu cereulid, se opětovně objevily v některých prodejnách Kauflandu, například v Jablonci nad Nisou. Státní zemědělská a potravinářská inspekce (SZPI) to zjistila při cílené kontrole tří prodejen společnosti.</description></item><item><title>Víte, zda vaše dítě sedí v autě skutečně bezpečně? Přijďte to zjistit do OC NISA</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902951-vite-zda-vase-dite-sedi-v-aute-skutecne-bezpecne-prijdte-to-zjistit-do-oc-nisa.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902951-vite-zda-vase-dite-sedi-v-aute-skutecne-bezpecne-prijdte-to-zjistit-do-oc-nisa.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:56:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Doprava</category><description>Správně nainstalovaná autosedačka, správně usazené dítě a správně dotažené pásy – tři podmínky, které musí být splněny zároveň, aby autosedačka při nehodě plnila svou funkci. Přitom právě v těchto detailech rodiče nejčastěji chybují, aniž by o tom věděli.</description></item><item><title>V Liberci vyrostlo největší solární parkoviště v Česku. Je v areálu DENSO</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903139-v-liberci-vyrostlo-nejvetsi-solarni-parkoviste-v-cesku-je-v-arealu-denso.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903139-v-liberci-vyrostlo-nejvetsi-solarni-parkoviste-v-cesku-je-v-arealu-denso.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 16:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Největší solární parkoviště v ČR vyrostlo v areálu DENSO v průmyslové zóně v Liberci. Takzvaný carport tvoří 2 706 solárních panelů, jejich výkon bude 1,8 MWp, zaparkovat pod nimi může 482 aut. Firma tak využila parkoviště k výrobě zelené energie, zároveň zlepšila komfort parkování pro zaměstnance.</description></item><item><title>Arsenal má náhradu za odvolaného Mathausera. Přichází Chorvat Matić</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903138-arsenal-ma-nahradu-za-odvolaneho-mathausera-prichazi-chorvat-mati.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903138-arsenal-ma-nahradu-za-odvolaneho-mathausera-prichazi-chorvat-mati.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:42:09 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Českolipský Arsenal představil trenéra, který nahradí odvolaného Petra Mathausera. Do Česka přichází zcela nové trenérské jméno – sedmačtyřicetiletý Chorvat Stipe Matić. Ten má trenérské zkušenosti ze švýcarského Thunu. Naposledy pracoval jako skaut.</description></item><item><title>Zajímavost voleb. Hned několik obcí s lyžařskými středisky čeká výměna starosty</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903077-krkonosskou-rokytnici-benecko-vitkovice-a-asi-i-harrachov-ceka-vymena.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903077-krkonosskou-rokytnici-benecko-vitkovice-a-asi-i-harrachov-ceka-vymena.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 14:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nového starostu bude mít většina obcí se známými lyžařskými areály v Libereckém kraji. Jiného budou mít krkonošská střediska Rokytnice nad Jizerou, Benecko, Vítkovice a nejspíš i Harrachov. V jizerskohorském Bedřichově možná zůstane stávající, povolební vyjednávání tam ale ještě neskončila.</description></item><item><title>Změna na průtahu. Směr na Prahu se uzavře, k OC Nisa a na Dlouhý most nesjedete</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903085-zmena-na-prutahu-smer-na-prahu-se-uzavre-k-oc-nisa-a-na-dlouhy-most-nesjedete.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903085-zmena-na-prutahu-smer-na-prahu-se-uzavre-k-oc-nisa-a-na-dlouhy-most-nesjedete.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:57:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Už v sobotu dojde k další změně v omezení na průtahu Libercem. Půjde o opravovaný úsek mezi Makrem a sjezdem u benzínové čerpací stanice Čermák. Zavřený bude jízdní pás ve směru z Děčína na Prahu a doprava opět povede v protisměrném jízdním pásu v režimu 1+1.</description></item><item><title>Technické služby Liberce vybudují tři vrty, ušetří za pitnou vodu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903067-technicke-sluzby-liberce-vybuduji-tri-vrty-usetri-za-pitnou-vodu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903067-technicke-sluzby-liberce-vybuduji-tri-vrty-usetri-za-pitnou-vodu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Městské technické služby Liberce (TSML) vybudují tři vrty ve svém areálu v Otavské ulici. Ušetří díky nim za pitnou vodu, navíc budou mít jistotu zdroje, pokud by nastalo sucho a nemohly odebírat povrchovou vodu. Vybudování vrtů si vyžádá zhruba tři miliony korun.</description></item><item><title>Liberečtí policisté stopli milionový podvod. Falešný kurýr dojezdil</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903069-liberecti-policiste-stopli-milionovy-podvod-falesny-kuryr-dojezdil.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903069-liberecti-policiste-stopli-milionovy-podvod-falesny-kuryr-dojezdil.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:51:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Liberečtí kriminalisté dopadli třiadvacetiletého cizince, který jako kurýr přebíral peníze od oběti investičního podvodu. Žena muži postupně předala přes dva miliony korun. Při čtvrtém pokusu kontaktovala policii, která podvodníka zadržela přímo při předání. Nyní mu hrozí až pět let vězení.</description></item><item><title>Ve Frýdlantu je už po volbách jasno. Kdo bude starostou, místostarostou a v radě?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903065-ve-frydlantu-je-uz-po-volbach-jasno-kdo-bude-starostou-mistostarostou-a-v-rade.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903065-ve-frydlantu-je-uz-po-volbach-jasno-kdo-bude-starostou-mistostarostou-a-v-rade.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 15 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Povolební jednání ve Frýdlantu významně postoupila. Zástupci tří volebních uskupení: Frýdlantu pro všechny, Místních a SLK a Nezávislých pro Frýdlant uzavřeli ve středu večer koaliční dohodu. Starostou se podle ní má stát dosavadní místostarosta Jiří Stodůlka, místostarostou nováček Martin Roušal.</description></item></channel></rss>
